Great restaurant in a Dar within the Medina
Apr 2025 • Couples
We had dinner at Dar Belhadj the first night we arrived in Tunis, as suggested by the concierge of our hotel, as an alternative to the restaurant where we wanted to go, but which had no place.
Beautiful structure located inside the Medina. 
The room manager was very attentive and friendly.
We ate a plate of mixed appetizers to share followed by baked lamb and always lamb couscous. 
To close a plate of seasonal fruit and a lemon sorbet.
One of the few places inside the medina that serves alcohol.
High bill compared to average Tunisian prices, but cheaper than other similar restaurants

Do not hesitate, in the heart of the Medina, it is a niche restaurant worth the visit!!

Nice atmosphere, good music, friendly staff, mediocre food.
Mar 2025 • Solo
Note to self: don’t travel to a Muslim country during Ramadan. My bad; I get it. I can live without cafes being open during the day (almost) and without wine at dinner (almost), but that puts the pressure on the after sundown meal to be even more amazing. I didn’t make a reservation and the place was packed, so I waited about 15 minutes for a table. The menu was set and prix-fixe. The service was immediate (5 or 6 people swooping down with appetizers water etc). The main dish was the real problem: a slab of roast beef so dry it rivaled my mother’s for toughness. I ate the pasta side and just pointed to the beef/shoe and said, “impossible” (a French cognate) when the waiter came to pick up my plate. I guess the price was literally fixed because no one mentioned the beef and I paid my 90 dinar and left. 🤷🏻‍♂️
